rows.subtopic: A relationship's slow drift and breakup
rows.description: The partner notices fewer touches, less curiosity and separate evenings. She feels lonely inside the relationship, more than she would alone, and yet says nothing to avoid a difficult talk.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17

rows.subtopic: A relationship's slow drift and breakup
rows.description: One finally says "I feel we are drifting, and I am not sure how to bring us back." Saying it kindly out loud lets both decide whether to repair, try counselling or part with honesty.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17

rows.subtopic: A relationship's slow drift and breakup
rows.description: They try for a few months and honestly ask whether the wish to fix it is love or fear of being alone. Staying out of guilt, or leaving out of restlessness, both need looking at truthfully.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17
related mind states: affection, fear, guilt, boredom

rows.subtopic: A relationship's slow drift and breakup
rows.description: If they part, they tell families with agreed words, avoid blaming stories and divide shared things fairly. Grief and relief usually arrive together, and time, friends and routine carry a person through.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17
related mind states: admiration, grief, relief

rows.description: A teenager sees his girlfriend laughing with a classmate and feels his stomach tighten. The thought "she likes him more" arrives faster than any evidence for it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22

rows.description: He replays the scene, scrolls through her tagged photos and imagines the worst. Every ambiguous detail is read as proof, and looking for reassurance feeds the fear instead of easing it.
graph_context: previous stage: A threat is sensed
this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22

rows.description: He asks who she was with and demands to see her chats, sure that he only wants the truth. What he calls love feels to her like being watched, and she starts to hide small things.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22

rows.description: She feels guilty for innocent things and tiptoes around him, dropping friends to keep peace. Loving someone should not require shrinking one's world, and she may need a trusted adult's view.
graph_context: next stage: Naming the fear beneath
this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22
related mind states: guilt, calm, trust

rows.description: A wiser friend asks "what are you afraid of losing?" He admits he feels not good enough, so the real issue is his self-worth, and controlling her cannot fix it.
graph_context: next stage: Choosing trust or stepping away
this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22

rows.subtype: Stage 6: Choosing trust or stepping away [Response]
rows.description: He tells her honestly that he felt insecure and stops checking, or if the pattern will not stop, both accept the relationship is not healthy. Controlling behaviour is a signal to involve a counsellor or elder.
graph_context: previous stage: Naming the fear beneath
this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22
